title: Logspace computability of the reduction
statement: For every finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and every natural number $c_0$, the reduction output has length bounded by $C(|x|+1)^c$ for some natural numbers $C,c$ and every input bit string $x$. Moreover, both languages of indexed output bits and output positions—whose membership predicates respectively ask whether the bit at position $i$ is true and whether $i$ is less than the output length—are decidable in logarithmic space.
hypotheses_covered: a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
